key_insight: A physics-aligned simulator for deformable objects can act as a zero-shot data scaler: by generating diverse, physically plausible soft-body interactions, it enables policies trained only in simulation to transfer to real-world deformable manipulation without additional real data.
problem_solved: Bridges the sim-to-real gap for deformable-object manipulation caused by rigid-body-centric simulators, reducing the need for costly real-world data and brittle motion primitives.
method: Design a physics-aligned simulator that models shape, contact, and topology co-evolution for soft/deformable objects (e.g., cloth, soft bodies).
Use the simulator as a zero-shot data generator: produce diverse, physically plausible rollouts and motion primitives to train policies at scale without real data.
Align and validate simulator physics with real-world priors (calibration, constrained parameterization or lightweight domain alignment) to maximize zero-shot transferability.
impact: Enables large-scale, low-cost training for deformable manipulation tasks, improving robustness of learned controllers and accelerating deployment of soft-object robotics without extensive real-data collection.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: rigid-body simulator failure vs. physics-aligned deformable simulator success on the same cloth task.
Pipeline diagram: physics-aligned simulator → large synthetic dataset → policy training → zero-shot deployment on real robot.
Sequence frames or GIF of cloth/soft-body manipulation from sim to real to illustrate transfer fidelity.
Bar/line chart concept: relative real-data requirements or task success rates showing reduced real-data need and improved transfer.
paper_title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds
paper_authors: Yunsong Zhou, Hangxu Liu, Xuekun Jiang, Xing Shen, Yuanzhen Zhou
